_keying: Keyed on file + enclosing SYMBOL, never file:line. The first version used file:line and emptied itself the moment a resolver was inserted above the sites: six cited exemptions stopped matching and the census read 11 remaining / 2 exempt instead of 6 / 8. A symbol survives edits above it and deliberately does NOT survive a rename — a renamed tool should have to re-justify its exemption.
_the_legacy_trap_2026_09_03: I ALMOST EXEMPTED FIVE LIVE CODE PATHS AS 'LEGACY'. The census reports the enclosing SYMBOL, and five knowledge-service handlers carry legacy tool names: _handle_kg_build_graph, _handle_kg_build_wiki, _handle_kg_schema_edit, _handle_kg_adopt_template, _handle_kg_sync_apply. Their TOOLS are visibility:legacy and withheld from the model. Their HANDLERS are not: build_tools.py:273/284 route the LIVE kg_build into the two build cores, and graph_schema_tools.py:564-578 dispatch the LIVE kg_ontology_propose by `op` into the other three. A tool being legacy says nothing about whether its handler is dead. Excluding them would have made D4 pass over the minting path of two live tools. The census counting HANDLERS rather than tool names is what made this visible.
_a_grep_that_hid_its_own_answer_2026_09_: I FIRST RECORDED provider-registry AS HAVING NO LEDGER, AND THE CAUSE WAS THE COMMAND, NOT THE CODE. The check was `grep -iE 'jti|consume|single' ... | head -6`. `consume` also matches `consumer` — RabbitMQ consumers, event consumers — and six of those appear before `consumeSettingsToken` in file order. The true positive existed and was pushed off the end by its own pattern's false positives. A `head -N` over a pattern that matches a common substring does not sample the matches; it samples the FILE ORDER. Re-checked translation the same way afterwards with no truncation and read every hit — that one is genuinely ledger-free.
